correctness.rationale: Total visibility is reconstructed from the forbidden Hamming-distance-two condition by a monotone shortest-path argument. A halfcube is a 64-vertex distance-two graph; its closed balls have 22 vertices, pair intersections of size six at distance four and zero at distance six, and triple intersections of size one precisely for three pairwise distance-four centers. No independent triple dominates. For four independent centers, exact inclusion-exclusion yields neighborhood-union sizes 64, 60 or at most 56 according to whether two, one or zero pairs have distance six. Hence dominating quadruples are precisely two disjoint distance-six pairs. Double counting 7 choices of partner and 10 complementary triple partitions gives \(64\cdot70/4=1120\) per parity and 1120 squared globally. The independently executed complete enumeration confirms the exact cardinalities and the direct shortest-path checks confirm representative feasible sets; the proof covers every labelled Q7 configuration.

value.rationale: An explicit 2023 open problem asks for lower total mutual visibility on hypercubes. The exact dimension-seven value 8 and the 1,254,400 labelled achievers are a natural finite instance, not an arbitrary slice: they classify all smallest greedy terminal configurations of this graph, with an intrinsic geometric distance-six matching rule. Comparing to the known maximum 16 shows substantial nonpurity and a factor-two greedy endpoint gap. The exact count is not implied by the existing halfcube independence polynomial; the closed-intersection proof explains the difference rather than merely reporting an exhaustive table.
